The creation of the heavens and earth, night and day, ships at sea, rain reviving the earth, creatures, winds and clouds are signs for people who use reason.
The creation of the heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding.
Allah splits grain and seed, brings the living from the dead, makes the night, sun, moon and stars, produced people from one soul, and sends rain for crops and fruit.
Allah sends winds and rain to a dead land and brings forth fruits, and so He will bring forth the dead; good land yields growth, bad land only sparsely.
Allah made the sun a shining light and the moon a light with phases for counting years; the alternation of night and day and all He created are signs.
Allah made the night for rest and the day for sight; in that are signs for people who listen.
Allah raised the heavens without visible pillars, subjected sun and moon, spread the earth with mountains, rivers and fruits, and makes crops watered by one water differ; these are signs.
Allah created the heavens and earth, sends rain for fruits and subjected the ships, rivers, sun, moon, night and day; His favors cannot be counted, yet mankind is ungrateful.
Allah placed stars in the heaven, protected it from devils pursued by flames, spread the earth with mountains and means of living, and sends winds and rain in known measure.
Allah sends rain and grows crops, and subjects night and day, sun, moon, stars and the sea; He set mountains, rivers, roads and landmarks so people are guided.
Rain revives the dead earth, livestock give pure milk, palms and vines yield intoxicant and good provision, and the bee, inspired by its Lord, produces a healing drink.
Allah gives people hearing, sight and intellect, holds the birds aloft, and provides homes, tents, shade, shelter and garments; they recognize His favor, then deny it.
Allah made night and day two signs, the day visible so people can seek His bounty and count the years, and He has set out everything in detail.
The heavens and earth were joined and parted, every living thing was made from water, and Allah made mountains, a protected sky, night and day, and orbiting sun and moon.
Allah merges night and day, sends rain that greens the earth, owns all, subjects the earth and ships to people, holds up the sky, and gives life and death.
Allah created seven heavens and sends measured rain, bringing forth palms, grapevines and an oil tree from Mount Sinai, and gives livestock for drink and food, and ships for carrying.
Allah gave people hearing, sight and hearts, spread them through the earth to be gathered to Him, gives life and death and alternates night and day, yet few are grateful.
Allah drives clouds that bring rain and hail, alternates night and day, and created every creature from water, some moving on bellies, some on two legs, some on four.
Allah extends the shadow, makes night a covering, sleep a rest and day a resurrection, and sends winds and pure water to revive dead land and water livestock and people.
Allah released two seas, fresh and salty, with a barrier between them, and created humans from water, joined by lineage and marriage.
Allah placed great stars, a burning lamp and a luminous moon in the sky, and made night and day succeed each other for those who remember or give thanks.
The earth produces every noble kind, a sign most do not believe, and the Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
If Allah made night or day endless until the Day of Resurrection, no other deity could bring light or rest; in mercy He made both for rest and bounty.
Among Allah's signs are humans made from dust, mates who bring tranquillity, varied languages and colors, sleep, lightning and rain, and the heavens and earth standing by His command.
Among Allah's signs are the winds bringing good tidings and mercy, and letting ships sail by His command so people may seek His bounty and perhaps be grateful.
Allah's winds bring rain on whom He wills after despair, reviving the earth as He will revive the dead, yet if a wind yellowed their crops they would disbelieve.
Allah merges night into day, runs the sun and moon, and sails ships to show His signs; amid waves people call on Him sincerely, but once ashore some stay moderate.
Allah drives water to barren land and brings forth crops that feed their livestock and themselves, if they would see.
The fresh and salty waters are not alike, yet from each people eat tender meat and take ornaments, and ships plow through them as people seek His bounty.
Rain brings fruits of many colors, and mountains, people, creatures and livestock also vary in color; only those of His servants with knowledge fear Allah.
Signs for them include the revived dead earth with grain and gardens, night, the sun and moon each set on its course, and the laden ship that carried their forefathers.
Allah created and tamed livestock for people to own, ride and eat, with other benefits and drinks, so they should be grateful.
Allah adorned the nearest heaven with stars as protection from every rebellious devil, which cannot listen to the exalted assembly and is pelted and pursued by a piercing flame.
Allah made night for rest and day for sight, the earth a settlement and the sky a ceiling, and formed and provided for people; He is Creator of all things.
Allah made grazing animals for riding, eating and other benefits, and ships to carry people; these are His signs, and they are asked which of them they deny.
Night and day, the sun and moon are His signs, so prostrate to Allah, not to them; rain reviving the still earth shows He gives life to the dead.
Among Allah's signs are the creation of the heavens and earth and the creatures He dispersed in them, and He is able to gather them when He wills.
Ships like mountains are His signs; He could still the wind or destroy them for what they earned, but pardons much, and disputers of His signs have no escape.
They admit the Exalted, the Knowing created the heavens and earth; He made the earth a bed, sends rain, and gave ships and animals to ride, exalting Him when mounted.
The heavens and earth, people and creatures, night and day, provision sent from the sky to revive the earth, and the winds are signs for those who believe and reason.
Allah subjected the sea for ships and all in the heavens and earth to people, signs for those who give thought.
The built and adorned heaven, the spread earth with mountains and plants, and rain bringing gardens, grain and palms to dead land are reminders, and thus is the resurrection.
There are signs on earth and in yourselves, and in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised; by the Lord of heaven and earth, it is true.
The sun and moon move by precise calculation, and the stars and trees prostrate.
Allah laid out the earth for the creatures, with fruit, palm trees, grain and scented plants, then asks which of your Lord's favors you would deny.
He is Lord of the two sunrises and two sunsets, released the two seas with a barrier between them yielding pearl and coral, and owns ships like mountains.
Allah asks who grows the sown seed, sends down drinking water and produced the tree for fire; He could ruin crops and water, so exalt the name of your Lord.
Only the Most Merciful holds birds aloft, aids and provides; He produced people with hearing, sight and hearts, spread them over the earth and will gather them.
People are asked who could bring them flowing water if their water sank into the earth.
Allah made the earth a container for the living and the dead, set lofty mountains and gave sweet water to drink; woe that Day to the deniers.
Allah made the earth a resting place, mountains as stakes, people in pairs, sleep for rest, night and day, seven heavens, a burning lamp, and rain for grain and gardens.
Man should consider his food: Allah pours rain, splits the earth and grows grain, grapes, olives, palms, gardens, fruit and grass for people and their livestock.
People are asked to look at how camels are created, the sky raised, the mountains set up and the earth spread out.
